title: What If Light Bulbs Were Built to Fail? A Cartel Agreed On It

scenes.text: What if the world's biggest bulb makers agreed to make their bulbs die sooner? They did.
On Christmas Eve 1924, firms like Osram, Philips and General Electric's foreign arms formed the Phoebus cartel.
They set bulb life at 1,000 hours, and fined members whose bulbs lasted longer in a Swiss lab test.
Some bulbs before that had lasted up to 2,500 hours.
By 1933, the average lifespan had dropped to 1,200 hours.
Meanwhile a bulb in a California fire station has burned since 1901. The cartel ended in 1940.
